package.title: UX: Infinite Canvas System for Spatial Package Organization
package.summary: The Upgrade Publisher today renders its 8 deep-analysis packages as a flat vertical card list (src/app/page.tsx:313). That works for sequential reading but hides the relationships between packages - which depend on each other, which touch the same files, which order to apply them in. This package introduces an infinite, user-configurable canvas: a 2D workspace where packages, findings, notes, and groups live as nodes; dependencies and conflicts live as edges; and every visual + behavioral dimension is driven by a hot-reloadable config object. Adds a minimap, find palette, templates library, PNG/SVG/JSON export, local-first persistence with version history, and a CRDT-ready collaboration foundation.

findings.title: Flat card list hides package relationships - no spatial overview exists
No infinite pan/zoom workspace - users cannot lay out artifacts spatially
No user-configurable theme/layout/behavior - one size fits nobody
No node-type extensibility - cannot add custom artifact kinds (notes, screenshots, embeds)
No keyboard-first / vim-modal canvas interaction - mouse-only is a power-user blocker
No persistence of canvas state - layout is lost on refresh
No templates library - every user rebuilds common layouts from scratch
No minimap / bird's-eye navigator - users get lost on large canvases
No find / command palette - cannot locate a node by name across a large canvas
No export to PNG/SVG/JSON/PDF - cannot share canvas outside the app
No spatial bookmarks / camera positions - cannot save and jump to views
No collaboration foundation - single-user only, no real-time multi-edit
